kpis.label: Operating earnings
kpis.note: −30% YoY — the number Buffett says matters

oneTimers: Other-than-temporary impairments: Berkshire wrote down its equity-method stakes in Kraft Heinz and Occidental Petroleum by $4.5B after tax in the quarter ($8.3B for the full year). The charge sits inside equity-method earnings, not operating earnings.

Investment gains are mostly paper gains: $9.6B of the quarter's $13.5B after-tax investment gains were unrealized — stocks Berkshire still owns went up in value. Next quarter they can just as easily go down.
'Other' operating earnings included about $617M of foreign-currency gains on non-dollar debt, versus $1.2B a year ago — one reason that line fell from $1.8B to $159M.
otherDetail: Investment gains of $17,210M — mostly paper gains on Berkshire's stock portfolio — less $5,301M of equity-method losses, driven by write-downs of the Kraft Heinz and Occidental stakes, and $68M attributable to noncontrolling interests.

takeaways.text: The businesses themselves earned $10.2B after tax, down from $14.5B — insurance underwriting dropped to $1.6B from $3.4B, and insurance investment income fell to $3.1B as interest rates came down.
takeaways.title: Operating earnings fell 30%

takeaways.text: Investment gains of $13.5B after tax — $9.6B of it unrealized gains on stocks Berkshire still holds, plus $3.9B realized on sales — turned a soft operating quarter into $19.2B of headline profit.
takeaways.title: Paper gains did the heavy lifting

takeaways.text: Berkshire recorded $4.5B of after-tax write-downs on its Kraft Heinz and Occidental Petroleum stakes — an admission both are worth less than it paid — inside equity-method losses of $5.3B before tax.
takeaways.title: Two big stakes written down

verdict: Berkshire's operating earnings fell 30% to $10.2B as insurance underwriting halved — but $13.5B of after-tax investment gains lifted headline profit to $19.2B, about the same as a year ago.
